compareElements(this=rcx,int a=edx,int b=r8d) 0x1414f7ec0 (matched fn): ListViewer* at +0x8; chain START at +0x10; entries are 8 bytes (plain code address, no this-adjust); NO count: loop `mov rax,[rbx]; test rax,rax; je end; call rax(rcx=sorter, rdx=rowA, r8=rowB); add rbx,8; stop on non-zero result`, so the chain is ended by a null 8-byte entry; direction int at +0x60 (>0 ascending; result negated when <=0). 10 slots fit between +0x10 and +0x60 (mac: 10 slots of 16 bytes +0x10..+0xb0): (dirOff - chainStart)/entrySize = (0x60-0x10)/8 = 10 on Windows, same count as mac, last slot must be the null terminator. Raw entry k at sorter+0x10+8k. In code: slots = sorter+0x10 as uintptr_t*, entry = slots[k], isNull = !slots[k]; mac needs 2 words per entry, Windows 1. Proposed: O_sorterChain Windows = 0x10 and mac code `O_sorterChain - 8` becomes `chainStart` (0x18-8=0x10 on mac, 0x10 on Windows); entrySize 16 mac / 8 Windows

a and b are the two element POINTERS (db::RowDataTrack*) from ListViewer::getCurrentListTrack(row) 0x1414add90 (rdx=rbp=track(a), r8=r14=track(b)), same as mac (rsi,rdx). Entries are called as `call rax` with rcx=sorter unmodified; setCompFunc 0x1414f7990 and setCompareFuncTo 0x1414fa4a0 store raw code addresses ([this+idx*8+0x10]=r8); all 39 distinct lea-targets in setCompFunc/setCompareFuncWithArtistAndAlbum (0x1414fa3d0) are real function bodies (checked: none begins with the vcall-thunk 'mov rax,[rcx]' pattern). mac uses adj=0 non-virtual too, so calling entry(sorter,a,b) directly is correct.
